what_happened: The person running Athena saw in the drain log that the batch-ordering test "a group of urgent items does not start ahead of the improvement turn" did not finish its shard again. This time it rejected a third unrelated job, the "tokens loaded per class of work" status measure, which cost $5.23. The steward's item to fix this test was filed on 12 Nov and still has no decision. No job id is on the event. The fields do not say whether the test hangs, is slow or fails an assertion.
cause: A test shard that does not finish leaves no record of which test ran, how long it ran, or whether it hung or failed an assertion. Nothing tracks a test that fails across unrelated jobs, so a known-bad test keeps rejecting correct work. Nothing quarantines or retries such a test, and the fix item sits undecided. Each rejection is charged to the job rather than the test.
other_causes: The steward's fix item for this test has had no decision for about a day, so the known fault stays live.
Athena does not count repeated rejections by the same test across jobs. The third rejection was noticed by a person reading the drain log.
open_hypotheses: The test is slow or timing-dependent and exceeds the shard deadline under load.
The test hangs on a real defect in the batch-ordering code, not on timing.
Disk or CPU contention from parallel jobs makes the shard stall.
contradictions: The event lists the rejected job as a status-measure change, which is unrelated to drain ordering. That fits an unrelated flaky test. It also means the jobs themselves are probably not at fault, so the test gate's verdicts here are not reliable.
prevention: Add a code check that does two things. First, when a test shard does not finish, it records the unfinished test name and its elapsed time in the kept output, and labels the result as a timeout rather than a failure. Second, it counts, per test, how many unrelated jobs it has rejected. At two or more, it reruns the job's checks on a clean baseline. If the test also fails there, it marks the test as known-bad, files the fix at high priority, and does not charge the rejection to the job. This would have kept the first two rejections from repeating.
proposed_request: Fix the test 'a group of urgent items does not start ahead of the improvement turn' so it passes reliably and finishes well inside its shard deadline. It has caused three unrelated jobs to be rejected because its shard did not finish. First, run the test alone on the current main several times and record whether it hangs, runs slowly or fails an assertion, with timings. Name the root cause in the changelog. Then fix that cause in the test or the batch-ordering code. Do not add a retry or a longer timeout alone. Also make a test shard that does not finish record the name of the unfinished test and its elapsed time in the kept check output. Acceptance: the test passes in 20 consecutive runs, the shard finishes within its deadline, and an unfinished shard's kept output names the test.
